answer: A significant way I have changed over the last few years is that I have become far more patient and self-assured. In my younger days, I was quite [[impulsive]] and would get frustrated easily when things did not go my way. At university, I would argue with friends over the smallest things and make hasty decisions I later regretted. I think this change came about through a combination of life experience and facing a few genuine challenges. Starting work played a big part, because dealing with worried students and demanding deadlines forced me to stay calm. Around the same time, my father retired, and I found myself taking on more responsibility at home. Overcoming difficulties taught me that most problems are temporary and that panicking rarely helps. As a result, I now approach setbacks far more calmly and rationally. This shift has affected me profoundly; I feel more [[grounded]] and less anxious than I used to. It has also improved my relationships, as I listen more and react less. Honestly, I am genuinely pleased with this change, because it has made me a more balanced person. I think personal growth like this is one of the quiet rewards of getting older. I no longer [[sweat the small things]] the way I once did. My mother says I have become more like my grandfather, which I take as the highest compliment. It is a change I am proud of, and it is genuinely [[liberating]] to feel this much calmer, as though a weight has been lifted from my shoulders.

followUps.q: Did anyone help you make this change?
followUps.answer: My grandfather, in a quiet way. Whenever I got worked up, he would just smile and tell me that no problem lasts forever. Seeing how calm he stays, even in his eighties, taught me a lot.

followUps.q: Is there anything about your younger self you miss?
followUps.answer: Perhaps a little of the fearlessness. When I was younger, I would try things without overthinking. Now I am more cautious, which is sensible, but occasionally I wish I were more [[spontaneous]].

note: Added university example, work and father's retirement as causes, effect on relationships and grandfather comparison; plain 'temporary' mark moved to sir's [[sweat the small things]].
